source_snapshot.procedure: During Test is TBD; source boilerplate says clear logs before testing and collect results/photos afterward.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED interprets the title as vendor session inventory. The exact workbook sequence—Get Session Challenge, Active Session, Set Session Privilege Level—maps instead to standard IPMI commands 39h, Activate Session 3Ah and Set Session Privilege Level 3Bh.

old_problem: Historical review assumed `Active Session` meant enumerate active sessions and therefore required a vendor inventory API, fields and pagination. Direct source-order and official-command analysis shows the likely source label omits `-ate`: row 1016 sits exactly between Get Session Challenge and Set Session Privilege Level in the IPMI Messaging Support Commands sequence. The missing Procedure/Criteria can be restored from standard Activate Session semantics without inventing an OEM API.
disposition_reason: Treat the preserved item text `Active Session` as the row label and implement the standard Activate Session App 3Ah checkpoint proven by adjacent command order. On a legacy IPMI 1.5 channel explicitly allowed by Project security policy, obtain a challenge/temp ID for a dedicated account, construct one authenticated Activate Session request with matching auth type, bounded maximum privilege and nonzero initial outbound sequence, validate the authenticated response/session ID/inbound sequence/max privilege, send at most one harmless read to prove the session works, then Close Session and verify removal. No inventory dump, privilege escalation, production identity, raw secret capture or retry is used. If the legacy path is intentionally unsupported, authoritative capability/policy evidence permits N/A.
decision_basis: XLSX rows 1015-1017, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Row 1016 is unique, and formal queue sequence 59 is row 1017 / variant c4325cfeb9ab3a76.

The physical sequence is semantically exact: Get Session Challenge (App 39h), `Active Session`, then Set Session Privilege Level (App 3Bh). Official IPMI assigns App 3Ah between them as Activate Session; interpreting row 1016 as inventory would break the standard command ordering and duplicate later Get Session Info semantics.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.17/Table 22-22 requires the request session header authentication type from the corresponding challenge, null pre-session sequence, temporary Session ID, and an AuthCode unless type None. Payload bytes are auth type, requested maximum privilege, sixteen-byte challenge and nonzero four-byte initial outbound sequence LS byte first.

The auth type must match the challenge and session header. Requested maximum privilege must not exceed both channel and user limits and becomes a ceiling for the session; this row does not authorize later elevation or the adjacent Set Session Privilege Level test.

On success the authenticated response supplies the remainder-session auth type, possibly changed active Session ID, nonzero initial inbound sequence for multi-session channels and allowed maximum privilege. Named failures 81h-86h distinguish slot exhaustion, user/privilege resource limits, sequence range, invalid temp ID and excessive requested privilege.

The first active-session packet must use the assigned nonzero Session ID and inbound sequence; sequence values are then incremented per direction. A read-only Get Device ID plus an immediate Close Session proves operation and cleanup without changing configuration.

ED-03/ED-13 support exact standard BMC contracts and forbid OEM guesses; ED-15 governs unsupported legacy N/A; ED-18/ED-30 prohibit invented auth policy; ED-19 preserves audit logs; ED-28 requires isolated authorized tooling/recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 impose package, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict boundaries.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Activate Session (App 06h/3Ah) legacy session establishment
test_case.purpose: Establish exactly one approved legacy IPMI 1.5 session from the corresponding Get Session Challenge, validate authentication, privilege ceiling, assigned identifiers and inbound/outbound sequences, prove one harmless authenticated read, then close only that test session and restore the pre-test active-session/audit state.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware/channel and Project policy explicitly permitting the optional legacy IPMI 1.5 Activate Session path; Get Channel Authentication Capabilities and q57-compatible challenge support evidence
Dedicated ephemeral least-privilege account, exact user/channel privilege limits and selected standard authentication type; OEM auth 5h requires vendor algorithm authority and is otherwise excluded

Validated protected IPMI 1.5 session harness implementing section 22.17.1 AuthCode exactly, volatile challenge/key handling, nonzero random starting sequence, monotonic per-direction sequence tracking, response authentication and secret-safe redaction

Bounded request matrix: one successful Activate Session at the minimum privilege needed for Get Device ID and Close Session; no privilege escalation/negative fuzzing, no production session or second activation
Pre/post active-session inventory or count, audit retention, exact new test-session correlation token, supported Close Session path and owner cleanup for timeout/ambiguous activation
Security point confirmation showing target, account, auth type, requested ceiling, current/free session capacity, observer access, close/revocation plan and no plaintext secret exposure
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SECURITY-CONFORMANCE PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit/session inventory and verify free capacity; do not clear logs. Obtain one q57-standard challenge for the dedicated account. Display target/channel/auth type/requested privilege/nonzero outbound sequence/cleanup and obtain immediate approval. Build one IPMI v1.5 App NetFn 06h / command 3Ah request: session header uses the challenge auth type, null pre-session sequence, returned temporary Session ID and the exact spec AuthCode unless auth None; payload byte 1 repeats auth type, byte 2 is the approved maximum privilege, bytes 3-18 are the corresponding challenge, bytes 19-22 are a cryptographically generated nonzero initial outbound sequence LS-first. Keep all secret/key/challenge material volatile and emit redacted digests only. Require an authenticated 00h response, matching auth type, an assigned active Session ID, valid nonzero inbound sequence for a multi-session channel and allowed maximum privilege not above the request/user/channel ceiling. Using exactly the assigned inbound sequence, send one read-only Get Device ID; verify the response and sequence increment. Immediately send Close Session for only this correlated test Session ID, then prove it disappeared while all preexisting sessions remain. Zero volatile buffers and disable/dispose the test identity as approved. Never enumerate unrelated fields, set privilege, activate twice, retry on ambiguity, use production credentials, persist AuthCode/challenge/IDs, clear logs or close another session.
test_case.expected_result: Capability/policy permit the selected legacy path; challenge, auth type and temporary ID bind to the dedicated user. The single authenticated Activate Session returns 00h, valid authenticated response framing, matching auth type, assigned Session ID, valid inbound sequence and maximum privilege at or below all approved limits. One Get Device ID succeeds using the first correct active-session sequence and no unauthorized command is sent. Close Session removes only the test session; preexisting session inventory, management access and audit health remain unchanged. Sensitive key/challenge/AuthCode/raw identifiers are not persisted. A documented unsupported legacy path produces N/A, while 81h-86h or an auth/sequence mismatch is retained as FAIL/NOT READY evidence without retry.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact adjacent-command/3Ah identity, one authorized challenge-to-activation binding, correct request AuthCode/header/payload/endianness, nonzero outbound sequence, authenticated 00h response, assigned session/inbound sequence and bounded privilege, one sequenced harmless read, precise Close Session and verified non-mutation of other sessions/audit state. An inventory query alone, high-level login without packet evidence, auth mismatch, zero/out-of-range sequence, privilege above limits, unverified response signature, 81h-86h, production credential, raw secret/session logging, privilege change, unintended session, wrong closure, retry or incomplete cleanup cannot pass. Missing package means NOT READY; authoritative legacy omission is N/A.
safety_gate: Use only an isolated management network, dedicated ephemeral account and least privilege. Confirm current/free session capacity and independent administrator recovery before activation.

The harness must implement the exact standard AuthCode and sequence algorithm; do not hand-roll or guess OEM crypto, downgrade security, request Administrator unnecessarily or expose secrets via command line/process/logs.

One activation only. The specification permits retrying some activation packets, but this review forbids automatic retry; a timeout is ambiguous and must go to inventory/audit reconciliation and owner cleanup.
Redact challenge, key/password, AuthCode, raw Session IDs and source metadata. Preserve security/audit logs and preexisting session identities as protected comparisons; never clear them.
Send only Get Device ID and Close Session after activation. Do not invoke Set Session Privilege Level, configuration writes, inventory dumps or any other session-control operation.

Close only the positively correlated test session. Stop on slot exhaustion, auth/sequence mismatch, unexpected privilege, lockout/rate limit, management degradation or uncertain session identity, and let the security owner recover.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant and row-order mapping to App 3Ah; target/firmware/channel, legacy-policy and auth-capability evidence
Security approval, dedicated account metadata, user/channel privilege ceilings, harness/version/hash and AuthCode algorithm selection without secrets
Redacted challenge/temporary-ID correlation and Activate Session request structural proof: auth match, null pre-sequence, payload length, requested ceiling and nonzero outbound sequence
Authenticated redacted 00h response structural proof, assigned-ID correlation token, inbound/outbound sequence and permitted max-privilege checks
One sequenced Get Device ID request/response and exact sequence progression with no setting or privilege mutation
Pre/post session inventory/count, correlated Close Session, unaffected preexisting sessions, preserved audit/management health, buffer/test-identity disposal and engineer verdict/N/A authority
test_case.recovery: On timeout or an ambiguous Activate Session response, do not retry and do not assume no session exists. Preserve redacted audit evidence, use the independent observer to locate only the dedicated account/target/time-correlated session, and have the security owner close that positively identified session through the supported path. Never terminate by guessed Session ID or close unrelated operators. On secret exposure, revoke/rotate the dedicated credential and zero buffers; on slot/rate/auth degradation, stop and let the BMC/security owner restore policy. Verify preexisting sessions, audit integrity and management access before closure.

source_conflict.reason: Workbook adjacency and the official App command sequence resolve `Active Session` as Activate Session 3Ah, while retaining the original label for traceability. TBD procedure/criteria are completed in the Review layer; unsafe generic log clearing is excluded.

project_authority: The Project security/BMC owners approve legacy applicability, auth type, isolated account, privilege ceiling, harness, session capacity, redaction and exact cleanup. They issue PASS/FAIL/N/A and own ambiguous activation recovery; approval cannot permit production credentials, unverified crypto, retries, elevated privilege, raw secret/session disclosure, indiscriminate close or a high-level login without standard packet evidence.
